case_name: Kuldip Kaur And Ors vs State Of Punjab And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Kuldip Kaur and others (husband, wife, etc.)
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Punjab and another (wife's father?)

facts_of_case: Petitioners filed a petition under Section 13B of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The parties had an FIR registered against them in 2014. They reached a settlement/agreement dated 05.08.2014 and the matter was amicably resolved.

legal_principles.principle: A compromise between parties is the sine qua non in a modern society.
legal_principles.held: The compromise, in a modern society, is the sine qua non.
cited_cases: Kulwinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2007) 3 R.C.R. (Criminal) 1052

legal_principles.principle: A genuine compromise between parties is one arrived at out of their own free will, without any inducement, threat, promise, coercion or undue influence.
legal_principles.held: The compromise between the parties is genuine, arrived at out of their own free will, without any inducement, threat, promise, coercion or undue influence from any quarter.

outcome.final_order: The petition for quashing of FIR No. 4 dated 11.01.2014 under Sections 406, 498A, 307 IPC registered at Police Station Singh Bhagwantpur, District Rupnagar and all other consequential proceedings arising therefrom was allowed.

use_for_drafting: mediation and conciliation in family disputes
